## EXTRACT OF THE PRIVI-
## LEGE.

Permission is granted to Nicolas Chrestien, merchant Bookseller, & Printer in Paris, to print, or have printed, & sell, the book of the *Elements & astronomical principles* with the *universal judgments* of the same Astronomy. Likewise, a treatise on <term>elections</term> <note>The astrological practice of choosing the most auspicious time to begin a task or event.</note> of things to be done, or desired to be done, following the same, with several chapters serving the same, among others for <term>nativities</term> <note>The calculation and interpretation of a birth chart to determine an individual's destiny.</note> and for drawing up celestial figures. The whole composed by master Richard Roussat. And forbidden to all other Printers & Booksellers of this Kingdom, to neither Print nor sell the said book without the consent of the said Chrestien, for up to four years after the first printing of the same. And this under penalty of confiscation of the books & an arbitrary fine as appears more fully by letters from the King, given on this matter at Paris, the last day of September. In the year of grace 1551, signed by the council, Turpin, and sealed on a <term>simple tail</term> <note>A legal term (original: "simple queue") for a seal attached to a strip of parchment or paper hanging from the document.</note> of yellow wax.

->And the first printing was finished on the six-<-
->teenth of April, 1552<-

# Richard Rous-
## SAT OF LANGRES TO THE
->beloved Reader.<-

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'N' featuring the letter N set within a square border filled with stylized foliage and floral buds, possibly thistles.</image-desc> Do not be filled with wonder, human Reader, if I present to you this work—the treasure and much-desired secret of Astronomical science <note>In the 16th century, "Astronomy" and "Astrology" were often used interchangeably to describe the study of the stars and their influence on Earth.</note>—recently translated by me into the mother tongue and common French. For I was compelled to do this, both to satisfy the outcries and requests of some—indeed, pressed by those to whom I am greatly beholden as dear friends. I was also incited and stimulated by those good and virtuous spirits who are dedicated without rest to honest and restorative labor and study; those who are entirely insatiable in their desire to know by their very nature and to raise themselves toward perfection. This follows the saying of the Philosopher <note>A standard reference to Aristotle, the foundational authority for medieval and Renaissance science.</note> in the first book of his *Metaphysics*, and in the twelfth book of the same, where such similar words are found: "The work of nature is the work of intelligence and perfection" <note>original Latin: "Opus naturæ, est opus intelligentiæ, & perfectionis"</note>. I have not done this for troublesome spirits, poorly educated folk, or men who are not truly men: those who, day by day, in a sinister and perverse sense, interpret, comment upon, and explain (like simpletons and fools) the sayings and writings of others. Would that it were my will that all such people were, beyond comparison, more blind than moles and no less deaf than rocks. Furthermore, I have been emboldened, knowing that a short time ago, there was brought to light (and in the same language)...

<summary>In this preface, Richard Roussat introduces his translation of astronomical secrets into French, explaining that he did so at the request of virtuous scholars while expressing disdain for ignorant critics.</summary>
<keywords>Richard Roussat, Langres, translation, French language, Aristotle, Metaphysics, astronomical science, astrology, intellectual defense</keywords>

# EPISTLE

...the judgment of nativities <note>A "nativity" is a horoscope or astrological chart cast for the moment of a person's birth.</note>, and generally concerning the things required for such judgment. Furthermore, may it be your pleasure to take this small gift that I offer you into your hands, acting as its protector: valiantly repelling with your sturdy shield the assaults and insults of those far too dangerous serpentine tongues <note>A common 16th-century metaphor for slanderers or harsh critics.</note>. I most affectionately request you to receive it with a full and gracious countenance—indeed, with the same affection with which I present it to you—without, however, failing (if it seems good to you) to kindly excuse and amend any faults that might appear, with the sort of correction one gives to good friends. Praying, to conclude it all, that it be the Creator’s good pleasure to enroll you in the book of the living and grant you the enjoyment <note>original: "fruition," meaning the pleasure of possession or use of a benefit.</note> of eternal bliss among the blessed. So be it.

->End of the Epistle.<-

<note>Vocabulary from the original French: **natiuitez** (nativities/horoscopes), **Epistre** (epistle/letter), **beatitude** (bliss/blessedness), **Createur** (Creator), **fruition** (enjoyment/attainment), **iceluy** (this/the same).</note>

<summary>In this concluding portion of the dedication, Roussat asks his reader to protect his work from malicious critics and to offer friendly corrections, ending with a prayer for the reader's eternal salvation.</summary>

# CERTAIN PRELUDES AND
## NECESSARY PRINCIPLES
->for Astrology.<-

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'P' featuring a stylized lily flower inside a square decorative border.</image-desc>Firstly, it must be noted and known that in the circle called the <term>Zodiac</term><note>A belt of the heavens extending about 8 degrees on either side of the ecliptic, within which the sun, moon, and principal planets remain.</note>, there are twelve signs, or images; these signs are contained within the width and length of this Zodiac, otherwise called the "Sign-bearer" <note>original: "signi-fier," a term derived from the Latin *signifer*, meaning "carrier of signs."</note> because of the said signs. It contains a width of twelve degrees, namely six on one side of the line that divides the Zodiac into two parts, and six degrees on the other side of that same line, upon which, and through which, the Sun makes its movement without ever straying from it. This is called the <term>Ecliptic line</term><note>The apparent path of the Sun across the sky; it serves as the central line of the Zodiac.</note>. The other planets make their circuits and movements below and within the width of the aforementioned circle—namely the Zodiac—and sometimes approach one side and sometimes the other, without however passing outside the width of the said Zodiac.

Also, each sign is divided into thirty parts of the said degrees, and each degree has sixty parts called minutes, and each minute has sixty parts called seconds, and each second has sixty parts called thirds, and each third has sixty parts called fourths, and so on with the following fractions <note>The author is describing the "sexagesimal" (base-60) system of measurement, which was standard for astronomical precision in the medieval and Renaissance periods.</note>. The twelve signs listed below are: Aries (the Ram), Taurus (the Bull), Gemini (the Twins), Cancer (the Crab), Leo (the Lion), Virgo (the Maiden), Libra (the Scales), Scorpio (the Scorpion), Sagittarius (the Archer), Capricorn (the Sea-Goat), Aquarius (the Water-Bearer), and Pisces (the Fish). <note>original Latin: "Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpius, Sagittarius, Capricornus, Aquarius, Pisces"</note> And these must always be counted, whether starting with Aries (which is the first) or with one of the others following in order, or as they succeed one another in order.

# NECESSARY PRELUDES

Also, the opposite signs are: <term>Aries</term><note>The Ram</note> and <term>Libra</term><note>The Scales</note>; <term>Taurus</term><note>The Bull</note> and <term>Scorpius</term><note>The Scorpion</note>; <term>Gemini</term><note>The Twins</note> and <term>Sagittarius</term><note>The Archer</note>; <term>Cancer</term><note>The Crab</note> and <term>Capricornus</term><note>The Sea-Goat</note>; <term>Leo</term><note>The Lion</note> and <term>Aquarius</term><note>The Water-Bearer</note>; and <term>Virgo</term><note>The Maiden</note> and <term>Pisces</term><note>The Fish</note>.

Also, one must know the types of <term>aspects</term><note>The specific angular distances between planets that astrologers believe influence earthly events.</note> or gazes, which are five: namely, opposition, conjunction, the third gaze, the fourth gaze, and the sextile gaze.
**Opposition** is said to occur when two planets are in two opposite signs; for example: if one of the planets is in Aries and the other is in Libra, then such planets are opposite to one another, provided they are nonetheless at the same degree—as, for example, if one were at the fifth degree of Aries and the other were at the fifth <insert>or sixth</insert> degree of Libra.
**Conjunction** is said to occur when two planets are in the same sign and at the very same degree of that sign; for example: if two planets were at the sixth degree of Taurus, or at any other degree of that same Taurus.
**Third aspect** or gaze <note>Known today as a **trine**.</note> is when there are four full signs from one planet to the other, which makes <term>six score degrees</term><note>120 degrees (6 x 20).</note>.
**Fourth gaze** <note>Known today as a **square** or **quadrature**.</note> is the name given when there are three full signs from one planet to the other, which makes <term>four score and ten degrees</term><note>90 degrees (4 x 20 + 10).</note>.
**Sextile aspect** or gaze is said to occur when there are two full signs from one planet to the other, which makes sixty degrees.

Also, it must be known that each degree the Moon travels is worth two hours of our clocks.

Also, in the section of the **Images** <note>In this context, "Images" refers to the constellations or the pictorial representations of the zodiac signs.</note> toward or on the southern side, there are written (as has already been said) in the Zodiac the twelve internal signs; in which Zodiac, drawing toward the center, many Images are included. And when the books of judgments <note>Works of judicial astrology used for making predictions or horoscopes.</note> make mention of any of these, it is necessary to look in that section and at the sign in which the planet

->ON ASTROLOGY.<-

...will be, of which the <term>Book of Judgments</term><note>Likely referring to the *Liber Iudiciorum*, a common title for medieval and Renaissance treatises on judicial astrology used to predict future events.</note> shall speak.

Also, the twelve signs have four distinct natures, according to the four <term>complexions</term><note>Also known as the four humors or temperaments (choleric, melancholic, sanguine, and phlegmatic), which were believed to govern both the human body and the cosmos.</note>: namely, the nature of Fire, the nature of Earth, the nature of Water, and the nature of Air. And in the said Zodiac, there are three signs of each nature; for example: all the signs that form a <term>third gaze</term><note>Known today as a **trine** aspect (120 degrees).</note> or third aspect together are of the same nature within a <term>triplicity</term><note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element.</note>. For instance, <term>Aries</term><note>The Ram</note>, <term>Leo</term><note>The Lion</note>, and <term>Sagittarius</term><note>The Archer</note> are a triplicity which is of the nature of Fire, hot and dry. <term>Taurus</term><note>The Bull</note>, <term>Virgo</term><note>The Maiden</note>, and <term>Capricornus</term><note>The Sea-Goat</note> form another triplicity of the nature of Earth, cold and dry. <term>Gemini</term><note>The Twins</note>, <term>Libra</term><note>The Scales</note>, and <term>Aquarius</term><note>The Water-Bearer</note> form another triplicity, which is of the nature of Air, hot and moist. <term>Cancer</term><note>The Crab</note>, <term>Scorpius</term><note>The Scorpion</note>, and <term>Pisces</term><note>The Fish</note> form another triplicity, which is of the nature of Water, cold and wet.

Also, it should be known that the <term>Dragon’s Head</term><note>original Latin: "Caput Draconis"; the North Node of the Moon.</note> and the <term>Dragon’s Tail</term><note>original Latin: "Cauda Draconis"; the South Node of the Moon.</note> are nothing other than the cut, division, and intersection of two circles: namely, the upper circle through which the Sun moves and travels, and the circle of the Moon. And where the circle of the Moon cuts and intersects the circle of the Sun while moving toward the North, it is called the **Dragon’s Head**. And the opposite cut or intersection, where the Moon passes while moving toward the South, is called the **Dragon’s Tail**.

Also, it should be known that the twelve signs rise in twenty-four hours; and thus, each sign rises in about two hours, one taking more time and another less, depending on the diversity of the lands <note>This refers to the "oblique ascension" of signs, where signs take different amounts of time to cross the horizon depending on the observer's latitude.</note>. This occurs because of the slant of the circle of the signs of the said Zodiac, as is clearly seen on the <term>Astrolabe</term><note>A portable medieval instrument used by astronomers and navigators to tell time and determine the position of celestial bodies.</note> when setting or creating the twelve <term>houses</term><note>The twelve divisions of an astrological chart representing different spheres of life (e.g., health, wealth, marriage).</note>.

# NECESSARY PRELIMINARIES

It should also be noted that when the planets recede and go outside their small <term>epicycle</term><note>In the Ptolemaic system of astronomy used at the time, an epicycle was a small circular path a planet followed while it also traveled along a larger orbit. This was a mathematical way to explain why planets sometimes appear to move backward.</note>, against the signs and degrees already passed, they are <term>retrograde</term><note>From the Latin *retrogradus*, meaning "stepping backward." This refers to the optical illusion where a planet appears to move in reverse across the sky.</note> until such time as they go forward with the signs again. This can easily be seen in the <term>Almanac</term><note>A book or table containing astronomical data and the positions of celestial bodies for a given year.</note>; for example:
If **Saturn** were on a certain day at the eighteenth degree of **Capricorn**, and the next day it were at the seventeenth degree of the same sign of **Capricorn**, then **Saturn** would be retrograde: for it moves against the order of the signs and degrees passed.

It also should be known that the <term>aspects</term><note>Original: *regards*. It is also necessary to know that all aspects the **Moon** makes with any of the other planets, or several of them, before its opposition to those planets, are called **dexter**. And from its opposition to that same planet until its conjunction with the **Moon**, all aspects that may be are **sinister**.

Regarding the movement of the planets, it should be understood that **Saturn** completes its movement and circuit through the twelve signs once in thirty years. **Jupiter** in twelve years. **Mars** in two years, or thereabouts. **Sol** <note>The Sun.</note> does so in one year. The **Moon** completes its own through the said twelve signs in one month.

And when she moves fourteen or sixteen degrees per day, then she is called swift in her motion, and is fortunate and good.

Likewise, planets are fortunate and good when they depart from any good planets, by aspect or by **conjunction** <note>When two planets appear at the same point in the sky.</note>, and move toward another good planet: that is to say, toward its conjunction, or opposition, or another aspect.

Likewise, Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars are strong and fortunate and in a good state when they are **Oriental** <note>Rising in the east before the Sun.</note>: that is to say, when the Sun has moved away from them by conjunction enough that they are outside the Sun’s rays. And Venus and Mercury are powerful and in a good state when they are **Occidental** <note>Setting in the west after the Sun.</note> to the Sun: that is to say, when they have passed the Sun; for they are swifter in their movements than the Sun is when they pass one another. And for this reason, they are strong when they begin to be uncovered by the Sun’s rays.

Likewise, planets are fortunate and good when they are **besieged** <note>Original: *assiegees*. A condition where a planet is placed between two others, receiving the combined influence of its neighbors.</note> between two good planets, such that one is ahead of it and the other is after it.

<header>IN ASTROLOGY.</header>

Also, the Moon is Northern <note>Referring to the Moon's celestial latitude being north of the ecliptic.</note> when it departs from its conjunction with its North Node <note>original: "Caput Draconis," literally "Head of the Dragon." This is the point where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path moving northward.</note>, until it is in conjunction with the South Node <note>original: "Cauda Draconis," literally "Tail of the Dragon." This is the point where the Moon crosses the Sun's path moving southward.</note>, and from the South Node until the conjunction with the North Node, it is Southern.

Also, it should be considered that if a diurnal planet <note>A planet belonging to the daytime "sect," such as the Sun, Jupiter, or Saturn.</note> is in a nocturnal sign, or if a masculine planet is in a feminine sign, it does not lose its power at all, provided that it is in one of its houses <note>The specific zodiac signs where a planet has its primary residence or "rulership."</note> or its exaltation <note>A specific sign where a planet's influence is amplified or "honored."</note>, although its power may be somewhat diminished thereby.

It is to be known that when the planet has passed the degree of its *Head* <note>original: "Caput," referring to the North Node (☊), the point where a planet's orbit crosses the Sun's path moving north.</note>, written in this table, until it comes to the degree where the Tail of the Dragon <note>The South Node (☋).</note> is, it is **Northern**. ## WHY THE ALMUTEN IS IN
### *a chart, or otherwise.*

The **Almuten** <note>original: "Alimité." A corruption of the Arabic "al-mubtazz," referring to the planet that holds the most "dignity" or power over a specific point in a horoscope.</note> is the conquering <note>original Latin: "Vincens."</note> planet, or significator, and the strongest; one will recognize it in this manner, for example: Let the sixth degree of Aries be taken, of which if you wish to know what the Almuten is, you must first look at which [planet] is the lord of the house <note>The "ruling" planet of a zodiac sign.</note>. This you will see, as well as the rest that follows, through the tables of the **Ephemerides** <note>Books containing pre-calculated positions of celestial bodies for every day of the year.</note>; and to summarize it all, it appears that this is Mars, and for that reason, it has six strengths <note>original: "forces." In traditional astrology, these are numerical points assigned to planets based on their position.</note> there. Afterward, one must consider which planet is **exalted** <note>original: "exaulcée." Exaltation is a position of high honor for a planet within a specific sign.</note> in the said Aries, which is the Sun; and because of this, the Sun has four strengths in the said Aries by its exaltation. Afterward, one must look at who is the lord of the **Triplicity** <note>Groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note>, where you find that the lord of the Triplicity by day is the Sun; and for that reason, if the birth <note>original: "nativité."</note>, or the revolution, or question, or other undertaking is by day, it is the Sun who is the principal lord of this Triplicity, and therefore the said lord has three **dignities** <note>Rankings or honors that strengthen a planet's influence.</note>, or strengths, by way of the said Triplicity. Afterward, look at who is the lord of the **term** <note>original: "terme." Small subdivisions of the zodiac signs where different planets have influence.</note> where the sixth degree of the said Aries falls; it appears by the said table that it is Jupiter, and therefore Jupiter has two strengths, or powers there.

Also <note>original: "Item."</note>, the lord of the **face** <note>original: "face." A 10-degree subdivision of a sign, often called a decan.</note> is Mars, whereby Mars has one strength once again. Now, to return to our purpose—that is, to find the Almuten at the said sixth degree of Aries—one must look at which of the planets has the most of the aforementioned strengths or essential powers at the said sixth degree; for the one that has the most in number is the Almuten, which

Alheten <note>Likely a corruption of Al-Khayyat or a similar Arabic name; he is identified here as the "son of Sehel," referring to the famous 9th-century astrologer Sahl ibn Bishr.</note> son of Sehel, who approved this judgment and found it to be true, says that you should take [the measurement] from the degree of the Midheaven <term>Midheaven: the highest point in the sky at the moment of the chart, representing one's career and public standing</term> to the malefic planet <note>original: "l'infortune"; usually referring to Saturn or Mars, which were thought to bring challenges or endings</note> which is closer than the others, just as Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century foundational figure of Western astrology</note> showed in order to know the hours of the distances of the planets from the Midheaven; and give each of these hours one year, and that is how long the lord will last in his lordship. ### *lordship. Chapter 21*

Ptolemy says in this place that it is necessary to look at the beginning of the lordship by the planet that shall be lord of the dignity <term>dignity: an office, rank, or position of power</term>, representing the person for whom you are looking. [Ensure] that this planet is in a good place; for by chance we might find a good ascendant <term>ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the start of an event, representing the person or entity involved</term> and the Moon regarding the fortunates <note>planets like Venus and Jupiter, which were believed to bring good luck</note>, and yet the lord of the dignity will be falling <term>falling: also called "cadent," a weak position in the astrological chart that suggests a lack of power</term> or "under the rays" <note>original: "souz les Roys"—likely a scribal error for "sous les rais," meaning a planet is so close to the Sun that its influence is "burned up" or hidden</note>, or it will not aspect the ascendant, or it will be in the second or the eighth [house]; then we must judge that the lord will not fare well in that dignity, but there will always be hardships. And also when the lord of the dignity and the planet he represents shall be in its fall <term>fall: "cas," the specific sign where a planet's influence is considered at its weakest</term> or unfortunate, it signifies the same thing. And from this example: When Al-Hafiz <note>likely Al-Hafiz, the son of the famous 9th-century astrologer Sahl ibn Bishr (Sechel)</note> departed from Arason, the ascendant was Leo, and the Sun, which is its lord, was in Leo, and the Moon and Jupiter were at the midheaven <term>midheaven: "my ciel," the highest point in the sky, representing career, success, and public standing</term>; and Venus, who was lady of the midheaven, was in the second house, and her placement did not aspect the ascendant nor its lord, and he was never in that dignity without anguish and without hardship until the time he was removed from it. And it profited him nothing that Jupiter and the Moon were in the midheaven in Taurus <note>original: "thaurel"—the sign of Taurus</note>, despite the Sun being in the ascendant and the ascendant being Leo—which is a sign that pertains to lordship—therefore...

### TO KNOW OF HE WHO

But if it were of swift movement and **Oriental** <term>Oriental: a planet that rises before the Sun in the morning</term>, his journey will be hasty and brief and without labor. 

And I say that when the **Lord of the Ascendant** <term>Lord of the Ascendant: the planet ruling the zodiac sign that was rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the question</term> **applies** <term>applies: the movement of a faster planet toward a mathematical aspect with a slower planet</term> to the Lord of the House of Journeys, or the Lord of the House of Journeys applies to the Lord of the Ascendant, or to any planet **carrying the light** <term>carrying the light: a technical condition where a fast planet moves from a conjunction with one planet to a conjunction with another, "delivering" the influence between them</term> from one to the other, or that any of them **collects the light** <term>collecting the light: when two planets both move toward an aspect with a third, slower planet, which "collects" their combined influence</term>, or that the Lord of the Journey be in the Ascendant, or the Lord of the Ascendant in the House of Journeys, or that the Lord of his places and the lords of their dignities be distant from the **angles** <term>angles: the four most powerful houses in a chart (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th), representing the cardinal directions</term>, or when the Lord of the Ascendant shall be in the **seventh angle** <note>The 7th House, which represents the destination or the person being sought</note>: all these things signify that the journey will be brief.

## TO KNOW WHEN A KING
### departs from a city what will become of those he leaves in
### it. Chapter 47

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'P' featuring floral motifs inside a square border.</image-desc>

To solve truly this and similar questions, you must look to see if you find an <term>affliction: a "malefic" planet like Mars or Saturn that brings difficulty</term> <note>original: "infortune"</note> in the <term>twelfth house: the part of the zodiac chart representing hidden enemies, prisons, and self-undoing</term>. This will signify that those whom the King leaves in his place will face obstacles. If the misfortune comes from **Saturn**, the damage will be from theft, or from being drowned in water, or from sickness. This is understood to be the case if the affliction is not <term>received: a cooperative relationship between planets where one "hosts" the other</term> <note>original: "receue"</note>; for if it were received, it does no damage.

And if that affliction is in its <term>fall: the sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest</term> <note>original: "cheute"</note>, it signifies that this evil will be strengthened, especially if, along with that, the affliction is <term>retrograde: appearing to move backward in the sky, usually indicating delays or reversals</term>. If you find in the **second house** any of the <term>fortunes: "benefic" planets like Jupiter or Venus that bring good luck</term>, it signifies in every way the opposite of what has been said. 

Know also that when the <term>Lord of the Ascendant: the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> or the **Moon** is afflicted, it signifies sadness for the one who has departed on his journey. And if the affliction that harms the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is above the earth between the **Ascendant** and the <term>Midheaven: the highest point in the sky at the time of the chart</term> <note>original: "my ciel"</note>, it signifies that it is an obstacle that will come to him while going. If the said affliction is below the earth, the sadness will happen to him in his company. And if the affliction is between the **fourth** and **seventh house**, it signifies an obstacle on his path while returning.

When you are asked about wealth <note>original: "substance"</note> or an object beneath the earth made by human hands—such as buckles and other such things—take the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the specific degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question; it represents the person asking the question</term>, and calculate it as precisely as you possibly can. A portion of the ancient sages say that when you are asked for a man or a woman whether they will have children <note>original: "filz," literally "sons," though often used generically for children in this period</note> or not: Look at the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</term>, and if **Fortune** <note>likely referring to the Part of Fortune, a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity</note> has regarded it, and the **Lord of the Ascendant** has been in the ascendant, or in the tenth, or in the eleventh, or in the twelfth [houses], and you have found **Jupiter** in a good place, with the Lord of its **triplicity** <term>triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (fire, earth, air, or water)</term>, and it has not been **under the rays** <term>under the rays: a planet positioned so close to the sun that its influence is "hidden" or weakened</term>, judge that he will have children, and if it is a woman, she will conceive.

And if you have found the ascendant damaged by **infortunes** <note>infortunes: "malefic" planets, usually Saturn or Mars, which were thought to bring challenges</note>, and its Lord in bad places, and Jupiter falling from the **angles** <term>angles: the four most powerful houses in a chart (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th)</term> below the rays in the **house of death** <note>the 8th house, associated with mortality and inheritance</note>, this signifies few children, and that they will not live for a long time if he has any. 

Similarly, if the **Moon** was **afflicted** <note>original: "infortunée," meaning poorly positioned or aspected by Mars or Saturn</note>, it signifies that she will not conceive; and if you have found a **fortune** <note>a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> in the **House of Children** <note>original: "maison du filz," referring to the 5th house of the zodiac</note>, looking upon it, this signifies that he will soon have a child. If an infortune was in the House of Children, and [the other planets] have looked upon it, this signifies that he will not have children; and if you have found other witnesses signifying having children, judge that he will have them, but he will see them die. If you have found Jupiter in the **Eastern Angle** <note>the 1st house or Ascendant</note>, it signifies that he will soon have a male child, and if the said Lord of the Ascendant was in the **Western Angle** <note>the 7th house</note> in a good place, it signifies that he will have a son, but it will be late after his question.

# TO KNOW AT WHAT
## time the woman will give birth. Chapter 66

When you wish to observe the time of birth: Observe when **Mars** and the **Sun** will be joined with the lord of the **house of sons** <term>house of sons: the fifth house of an astrological chart, which traditionally governs children, pregnancy, and creativity</term>, and when the **Moon** will be with the lord of the hour, or with several of them, and that shall be the hour of birth. And assist yourself in this with the **fortune** <note>a "benefic" or lucky planet, such as Jupiter or Venus</note> that was present in the **question** <note>original: "question"; in horary astrology, this refers to the moment a specific question is posed to the heavens</note>, observing the **part of sons** <note>original: "partie des filz"; also known as the "Lot of Children," a mathematical point on a chart calculated by the distance between specific planets</note> by **attazir** <note>original: "attazir"; a method of "directing" a planet or point through the degrees of the zodiac to calculate the timing of future events</note> to the degree of the house of sons or to the degree of **Jupiter**, or its rays, and especially if **Jupiter** is between the [Part of Sons] and the house of sons. For then, when this **part** is applied with **Jupiter** by the degrees of the **ascensions** <note>oblique or right ascensions used in astronomical calculations</note>: And when it has been between those of said degrees, at that time she shall give birth, giving to each degree one day. And observe the **application** <note>the movement of a faster planet toward an aspect with a slower one</note> of that [planet] toward which it looks, and [if] it applies before the **conjunction** <note>when two celestial bodies appear in the same place in the sky</note> of the lord of the house of sons, for that likewise is the time of birth. And likewise observe when the **significator** <note>the specific planet representing the subject of the inquiry</note> of the question shall open its form, for that is the time of birth. And observe which of all these has the greatest **testimony** <note>original: "tesmoing"; the weight of evidence or influence a planet has in a particular chart</note>, and you shall judge according to it. And likewise take from the lord of the house of sons and know that when it is [positioned], give to each **sign** one month, and assist yourself with the other testimonies, and you shall judge according to what they do in conjunction, if God wills.

To know whether the birth will take place by day or by night: Look to the sign of the **ascendant** and its **lord** <term>lord: the planet that rules a particular zodiac sign</term>, and the **Moon**, and the planet that shall be in the **ascension** <note>the sign or planet currently rising on the eastern horizon</note>, and the lord of the **house of children** <term>house of children: the fifth house of an astrological chart, which traditionally governs offspring and pregnancy</term>. If all of these, or the greater part of them, are in **day signs** <note>the "diurnal" signs: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius</note>, then she will give birth by day; and if they are in **night signs** <note>the "nocturnal" signs: Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces</note>, she will give birth by night. And if they are in discord, take the strongest among them and judge accordingly. Furthermore, take the distance from the degree of the sons to the degree of its lord, and however many degrees there are, subtract that same amount from the degree of the ascendant, and observe where that number falls. If the sign to which it applies is a day sign, and its lord is also in a day sign, she will give birth by day; if the contrary, she will give birth by night. Regarding this aforementioned **part** <note>original: "partie"; referring to the mathematical "Lot of Children" or "Part of Sons" used in calculations</note>, judge similarly for male and female. Observe the lord of the house of sons, the **Moon**, and the **lord of the hour**, and this aforementioned part and its lord, and observe its **witnesses** <note>planets that provide supporting "testimony" or evidence for a prediction</note> and its **significators** <note>planets that specifically represent the subject of the question</note>. If the greater part of them are in a **masculine sign**, she will give birth to a male; if they are in a **feminine sign**, she will give birth to a female, and she will give birth by night. And if they are equal, such that there are as many masculine as feminine, she will give birth to a child who shall have the nature of both man and woman <note>a historical reference to an intersex or "hermaphroditic" birth</note> between day and night.

## TO KNOW IF THE POISON-
### ed person can recover or not. Chapter 69

To answer this inquiry, you must consider if you find the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: a mathematical point in a chart representing luck and well-being</term> joined with **benefics**, or if you find a benefic planet applying to it, or if they have any **testimonies** <note>testimonies: supporting evidence from various planetary positions that help a practitioner reach a verdict</note> with it; if so, say that he shall recover. If you find the contrary, judge the contrary. And if you find the ascendant in a **mortal sign** <note>mortal sign: a zodiac sign associated with death or physical decline in medical astrology</note> and a benefic beholds it, say that he shall recover; but if it is the opposite, he cannot recover.

To know if the poisoner is a man or a woman: Look at the **fourth house** <term>fourth house: the section of the zodiac chart representing the home, secrets, and the "end of matters"</term>, and what kind of sign is there, and who is the **lord** <term>lord: the planet that rules a specific zodiac sign</term> of that house, and which planet has its **exaltation** <term>exaltation: a specific sign where a planet’s influence is most powerfully and harmoniously expressed</term> within it, and the lord of its **triplicity** <term>triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element—fire, earth, air, or water</term>, and the lord of the **term** <term>term: a specific division of a zodiac sign where a particular planet has secondary influence</term> of the degree of the fourth house. # TO KNOW IF A
## woman has had a child or not. Chapter 72

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut drop cap letter 'C' featuring scrolling foliate and floral motifs within a square frame with a double border.</image-desc>
Consider in this matter **Venus**; if you have found her in **Aquarius** or in **Leo** conjoined with **Mercury**, say for certain that she never had a child. If you find her conjoined with Mercury, or in **Scorpio**, or in **Taurus**, she has a son. And if the malefics mix with the two benefics in moveable signs, she has bad children who are troublesome to her.

## THE JUDGMENT OF HE WHO
### *is cast out of his place.* Chapter 77.

Look into the cause and business of he who is expelled by the King at the hour in which this affair occurred, and proceed by considering the Moon. If you have found her **separated** <note>In astrology, a planet is "separated" when it has recently moved away from an aspect (a specific mathematical angle) with another planet.</note> from a **fortune** <note>A benefic or "lucky" planet, traditionally Jupiter or Venus.</note>, and have found a **fortune** in the **ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the specific moment of an event.</note> of that hour looking toward the Moon, judge that the cause of this person is addressed, the harm is diminished, and it comes to a good end; thus, he shall return to his land and to his place. If you find the Moon **separated** from an **infortune** <note>A malefic or "unlucky" planet, traditionally Saturn or Mars.</note>, and in the **ascendant** there was an **infortune** looking toward the Moon, judge that his cause will be damaged and will go ill, in such a manner that he will not have the [safety or] fearlessness to return to his land and his place.

And I say for he who is in doubt, look to the **lord of the ascendant** <note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign found on the eastern horizon at the time of the query.</note>; and if you find it looking at the **ascendant** and **applying** <note>A planet is "applying" when it is moving toward a specific mathematical relationship (aspect) with another planet or point.</note> to the **fortunes**, judge that this fear or dread shall not touch him, nor shall he have any grief or any anxiety from it. If the **lord of the ascendant** is in the twelfth, or sixth, or eighth, or second house, judge that from this cause he will have fear and doubt, and it will be of the nature of the sign in which the **lord of the ascendant** was located. And if, in addition to this, it **applies** to an **infortune**, he shall escape from this, and yet he shall not remain long in fear.

If the **lord of the ascendant** were in the **angles** <note>The four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st (Ascendant), 4th (Imum Coeli), 7th (Descendant), and 10th (Midheaven).</note>, and the **infortunes** of the **angle** are **retrograde** <note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky, often signaling a period of disruption or weakened influence.</note> and more evil and stronger than they could possibly be, the misfortune in this is if that planet were the **lady** <note>The ruling planet of a house.</note> of the eighth house; for then it signifies that the cause of the thing which the person fears is the death and destruction of the one who doubts. And I say this regarding him who is expelled.

### *hour one must take the ascendant for the*

# A Small Treatise on
## ELECTIONS. <note>In astrology, "electional astrology" is the practice of choosing the most auspicious time to begin an activity, such as a journey, a marriage, or a war.</note>
### Chapter One.

Velius <note>likely referring to Vettius Valens, a famous 2nd-century Greek astrologer whose works were widely translated and cited in the Middle Ages and Renaissance</note> says that when you cannot remedy the timing, and the Moon is destined to be unfortunate, place the misfortune on the lord of the ascendant <term>the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the chart</term>. When you cannot make all the significations <term>the planets or points that represent the specific matter being asked about</term> of the election favorable, always empower and direct the lord of the ascendant when a fortune <term>a "benefic" planet, typically Jupiter or Venus, believed to bring good luck</term> is in an angle <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a chart, which are the most powerful positions</note>, and especially at the mid-heaven <note>the highest point of the chart, representing success and public status</note>; do not worry about anything else. The profit that can come from a good election is small when the revolution of the year <term>a "Solar Return" chart, calculated for the sun's annual return to its birth position to predict the year's events</term> is bad, and it is the same in the opposite case. Mars does no damage to those who travel by water, just as Saturn does no damage to those who travel by land on the roads. Fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius; signs associated with stability and persistence</note> are abominable [for change], just as mutable signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces; signs associated with transition and movement</note> are favored. None but God can withdraw the harm of a misfortune <term>a "malefic" planet, typically Mars or Saturn</term> when it is far from an angle and is peregrine <term>a planet positioned in a sign where it has no "dignity" or home-field advantage, making it weak and unpredictable like a wanderer</term> in a sign diverse and contrary to its nature. Venus and the Moon are very powerful in the fourth [house] Southern, and greatly weak in the Eastern. When a misfortune <term>malefic</term> receives a fortune <term>benefic</term>, it does little damage. And especially if it is delivered from a gaze of enmity <note>an "aspect" or geometric angle of tension, like a square (90°) or opposition (180°)</note>, the misfortune of the planets increases greatly when they are in a foreign place. It is not advisable to fight or assail cities when the significator <term>the planet representing the target city</term> is the lord of the ascendant of the revolution of the year.

Afterward, you shall look to the nature of the thing you wish to begin, and which sign of the heaven is naturally suited to it; then align the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant <term>the planet that rules the sign on the eastern horizon</term> with that nature, and strengthen it as much as you can at the hour of the inception <note>the exact moment a project or journey is officially started</note>. And if you wish to know anything regarding a King, or a powerful and magnanimous man who is held in reverence by the people, join yourself to **Jupiter**. If you wish for it from laborers, whether those of the city or wherever you please, join yourself to **Saturn**. And if you wish for it from judges, or from knights, or from men-at-arms, join yourself to **Mars**. If you wish for it from women, or for buying and selling, or for legal cases <note>original: "causes"</note>, join yourself to **Venus**. And if you wish for it from women who hold authority <note>original: "seigneurie"</note>, join yourself to the **Moon**. And if you wish for it from writers or from merchants, join yourself to **Mercury**.

### LITTLE TREATISE

Afterward, when you wish to begin any work, strengthen the ascendant <term>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> and its lord <term>the planet that rules the rising sign</term>, and the Moon and the lord of its house <note>the planet ruling the sign where the Moon is currently located</note> by observing them: as Dorotheus <note>original: "Dorochius"; refers to Dorotheus of Sidon, an influential 1st-century astrologer</note> and other sages say regarding the bad conditions of the Moon in all beginnings and in all deeds; and know that the Moon has ten bad conditions. 

The first is when she is combust <term>literally "burned"; a planet too close to the Sun is considered weakened or blinded by its heat</term> before the Sun by twelve degrees, and as many after. However, when she is after the said Sun, she is of lesser harm. 

The second is when she is in the degree of her fall <term>the specific area of the zodiac where a planet’s influence is at its weakest</term>. 

The third is when she is in opposition to the Sun <note>the time of the Full Moon, which was sometimes viewed as a moment of excessive tension in electional astrology</note>. 

The fourth is when she is bodily conjoined to the malefics <term>the "unfortunate" planets, Saturn and Mars</term>, or in a square <term>an aspect of 90 degrees</term> or in opposition <term>an aspect of 180 degrees</term> to them. 

The fifth is when she is with the Head of the Dragon or with the Tail <term>the North and South Nodes of the Moon, where its path crosses the ecliptic</term> within twelve degrees, which is the limit of the eclipse. 

The sixth is when she is in the final degrees of the signs which serve as the terms <term>specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign</term> of the malefics. 

The seventh is when she is falling from the angles <term>located in "cadent" houses, which were thought to be less powerful</term>, or when she is in the *Via Combusta* <note>original: "voye bruslée"; the "Burned Path," a specific section of the zodiac from the end of Libra to the beginning of Scorpio considered highly unpredictable</note>, which is the end of Libra and the beginning of Scorpio; and this is the worst of the Moon's misfortunes, especially in marriages, and in all matters concerning women, in buying and selling, and in travels. 

The eighth is when the eleventh [house or place] of the Moon is with the malefics, or when she is contrary to her house <note>located in the sign opposite the one she rules (Cancer), which is Capricorn</note>, or when she does not regard her house with any aspect. 

The ninth is when she is slow in motion—which motions the sages call the "motions of Saturn"—and this is when the Moon moves in one day and one night by twelve degrees or less.

If you are the one whom the King wishes to **disturb** <note>original: "destourbier"; meaning to legal harass, hinder, or bring a case against.</note>, set the **Moon** in increasing light <note>A waxing moon, moving from New to Full.</note>, and let it and the **ascendant** <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the chosen moment.</note> be safe from any **infortune** <term>Infortune</term> <note>A planet considered naturally unlucky or malefic, traditionally Saturn or Mars.</note>. Also, place the lord of the ascendant in a good house and in a good relationship to the ascendant, and in any of its **dignities** <term>Dignities</term> <note>The strengths a planet possesses based on its specific location in the zodiac.</note>, and moving **direct** <note>Moving forward through the zodiac, rather than appearing to move backward in "retrograde."</note> or upright, and safe from the infortunes, whether the lord itself is a **fortune** <note>A lucky planet, like Jupiter or Venus.</note> or an infortune. And place the lord of the **seventh house** <note>In a legal context, the seventh house represents the opponent or adversary.</note> in bad positions relative to the ascendant, and let no fortune nor any of the **luminaries** <term>Luminaries</term> <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> look upon it. If another person wishes to disturb you alongside the King, and you wish to plead before the said King and show your reasoning, set the Moon to be dominated by light, and let the [opponent's] ascendant and its lord, and the Moon, be afflicted. And place the lord of the **fourth house** <note>Representing the end of the matter or the "home" position.</note> as a fortune in a good position relative to the ascendant and well-supported, for then your "house" will be made better and much stronger.

## ELECTION FOR BUYING
*estates. Chapter 26*

Keep **Mars** away from her aspects, and make the **fourth house** a fixed sign <note>original: "signe ferme"; the signs Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which were thought to provide stability and permanence.</note>. Ensure that the lords of the angular houses <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart.</note> are Oriental <note>Rising in the east before the Sun.</note>, increasing in their movements, and Northern while ascending. And when buying any kind of estate, make sure the fortunes <note>Benefic planets, specifically Jupiter and Venus, which bring good luck.</note> have dignity in the angles, especially in the **ascendant**, or that the **fourth house** is a fixed sign, and that the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> regard the **ascendant** and the **fourth house** with a good aspect, and that no retrograde planet is in the angular houses, nor that their significators <note>The planets that represent the buyer or the property in the astrological calculation.</note> are retrograde.

### Of the hour of Venus.

In the hour of Venus, it is good to ride horses, but do not enter a boat to travel by water. Gain <term>influence: original "domination"</term> during this time, and involve yourself in this hour of joyfulness and amusements, and for playing <term>chess: original "eschetz"</term>. ### Of the hour of Mercury.

Do not release prisoners. Begin to <term>build: original "edifier"</term> and dig ditches. Set your children to their <term>studies: original "doctrine"</term> so they may learn well how to write.

# ON ELECTIONS.

In the hour of the Moon, do not begin to **build**, nor cut cloth; give your son to schooling <note>original: "aux lettres"; referring to education or literary studies</note>, pursue your enemy in this hour, and go on a journey, but if you are outside your land, do not re-enter it in this hour.

### Of the hour of Saturn.

In this hour of Saturn, do not take medicines, nor cut robes, and do not wear new clothes; do not go before the King, nor also into a boat to travel by water. Conquer your fugitive enemy therein, and buy weapons, and write letters. Do not take **legal action** <term>legal action: original "plait"; a lawsuit or court plea</term> against anyone, nor bleed any veins, nor use **cupping** <term>cupping: original "ventouses"; a medical treatment using suction on the skin</term>. Whoever departs in this hour to go on a journey will face much peril and imprisonment, and will be delayed and far-flung on said journey; and if his journey is by sea, he will face great perils from the waves <note>original: "undes"</note> and diverse winds that will cast him into another country. Also <note>original: "Item"</note>, in this hour it is good to work the land and dig ditches; and whoever should fall ill, that illness will be long-lasting for the patient, and what is worse, in the end, it will cause death.

### Of the hour of Jupiter.

In the hour of Jupiter, honor Kings, perform marriages with women, and cut robes. Do not buy armor. Sow all seeds, plant all trees, and begin all **buildings**. Do not enter a boat, nor **let blood** <term>let blood: original "minue sang de veine"; the medical practice of bloodletting</term> from a vein. And whoever departs in this hour to go on a journey will have profit and also success in financial matters.

# OF THE PART OF FORTUNE.
## Chapter 47

It should be known that the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: a specific point in a birth chart or election used to represent prosperity and well-being, calculated based on the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant</term>, of which mention has been made, is found in this manner: observe whether it is by day or by night that you wish to find the Part of Fortune. If it is by day, you shall take the degrees that are between the degrees of the Sun, up to the degrees where the Moon is, including its degrees. That is to say, begin counting that many degrees from the degree of the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the zodiac sign and degree rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</term> according to the order of the signs; where that limit ends is the place of the Part of Fortune. And the **lord** <note>original: "seigneur"; refers to the planet that rules the specific zodiac sign where the Part of Fortune falls</note> of this degree is the lord of the Part of Fortune, as for example:

Suppose that the Sun is at twenty degrees of **Pisces** <note>original: "Pisces"; the Fish</note>, and the Moon is at the first degree of **Virgo** <note>original: "Virgo"; the Virgin</note>. You will find in this case the place of the Part of Fortune, assuming that it is by day and that five degrees of **Libra** <note>original: "Libra"; the Scales</note> is in the ascendant. Count the degrees from the Sun to the Moon according to the order of the signs, and you will find 160 degrees <note>Historical astrological texts occasionally contain slight mathematical errors or use different rounding methods; the distance between 20° Pisces and 1° Virgo is approximately 161°</note> between the Sun and the Moon, and then after, count—

## OF THE PART OF SUBSTANCE.
->Chapitre. 48<-

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'L' decorated with floral and foliate motifs.</image-desc>

The **Part of Substance** <term>Part of Substance: also known as the Part of Wealth or Lot of Fortune's Substance, an astrological point used to predict a person's material resources and livelihood</term> is determined in this manner, whether by day or by night: one must count the degrees from where the **lord** of the **second house** <note>original: "seigneur de la deuxiefme maison"; the second house in astrology governs personal finances and possessions</note> is, following the order of the signs, to the first degree of the second house; and then begin to count that number of degrees from the **ascendant**, and where the count is found to end, there is the **Part of Substance**. This **Part of Substance** signifies various cases and things; however, in general, it signifies profit, provisions, food, the possession of riches, and all things necessary to sustain the human body. And if it falls in a good place, it signifies an increase in the aforementioned and declared things; and if such a part falls in an ill place of substance, it signifies hindrance in the aforementioned and fully declared things.

### Chapter.

#### Firstly, concerning the Part of the Moon.

The **Part of the Moon**, otherwise called the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: a sensitive point in a chart representing prosperity, health, and the physical body</term> is taken by day from the **Sun** to the **Moon**, and by night in the opposite direction, and is counted from the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>; that is to say, one must begin counting from the ascendant.

#### Concerning the Part of the Sun.

This **Part of the Sun**, which is the **Part of things to come** <note>original Latin: "futurorum"; also known as the Part of Spirit, representing the soul, will, and future intentions</note>, is taken by day from the **Moon** to the **Sun**, and by night from the **Sun** to the **Moon**, and is counted from the **ascendant**.

#### Concerning the Part of Saturn.

This **Saturnian Part** is a **heavy part** <note>original: "partie pondereuse"; reflecting Saturn's traditional nature as the 'heavy' or 'slow' planet associated with burdens and gravity</note>, and is taken by day from the degree of **Saturn** to the degree of the **Part of Fortune**, and by night in the opposite direction, and is counted from the **ascendant**.

#### Concerning the Part of Jupiter.

The **Part of Jupiter**, which is the **Part of happiness** <note>original: "beatitude"</note> and of **assistance**, is taken by day from the **Part of things to come** to **Jupiter**, and by night in the opposite direction, and is counted from the **ascendant**.

#### Concerning the Part of Mars.

This **part of collection**, which concerns gathering, is taken by day from **Mercury** (or the degree of said Mercury) to **Venus**, and by night the opposite, according to the order of the signs, and is counted from the ascendant; and one must do the same for the others, namely using the degree they hold within the sign in which they are located.

### TO UNDERSTAND THE MEAN MOTION of the Moon compared to her true motion.
#### Chapter 62

It should be known that the mean motion <term>mean motion: the average speed of a celestial body as if it moved in a perfect circle at a constant rate, used as a mathematical baseline</term> of the Moon for one day is thirteen degrees and ten minutes; therefore, when she travels more than thirteen degrees and ten minutes, her true motion <term>true motion: the actual, observed position and speed of a planet, which varies due to its elliptical orbit and distance from Earth</term> will exceed her mean motion. And if she travels less than thirteen degrees, her mean motion will exceed her true motion; this can be determined by using an almanac <note>In this period, an "almanac" was a set of tables predicting the daily positions of celestial bodies.</note>.

But to know which of the houses—for each of the planets has two houses, except for the Sun and the Moon <note>The Sun rules only Leo, and the Moon rules only Cancer</note>—it is to be known that the house which rose with them is the one whose nature the character of the inhabitants most closely resembles. Likewise, another way and method to find the ascendant and its lord <term>lord: the planet that governs the sign appearing on the eastern horizon</term> of any town, city, or castle is by one of the great conjunctions <note>Great conjunctions: specifically the meeting of Jupiter and Saturn, which historical astrologers used to predict major shifts in kingdoms and the fate of cities</note>. Such a planet as has signified the event is the lord of the town, city, or castle; and consequently, one of the houses of that same planet was at the ascendant during the foundation of that city, town, or castle. Thus, the Astrologers say that the "evil" planets <note>Traditionally Saturn and Mars</note> guard their own and kill the others. 

Furthermore, although Saturn may be the lord of a city and may guard that city from mortality, this must be understood with a condition: when Saturn, in the revolution of the year of the world <term>revolution of the year of the world: a specialized astrological chart cast for the moment the Sun enters Aries, used to predict the year's events for nations and cities</term>, is very strong and in a good place and state, then he has the power to guard his own. But if, in the revolution of the year of the world, he is weak and in a bad place, he has no power to guard his own. Supposing that Saturn is in conjunction with Jupiter, this signifies mortality in that year; therefore, mortality sometimes comes even to cities of which Saturn is the lord, for the reason stated above. ### On the Part of Retribution.

### On the Parts of Prosperity.

### *houses by another method.*

When you have your four <term>angles</term> <note>The four most important houses in a chart: the 1st (ascendant), 10th (midheaven), 7th (descendant), and 4th (lower midheaven)</note>, namely the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth houses, divide the semi-arc of the day <note>The portion of the sky the sun travels through from the horizon to the meridian</note> which is from the ascendant until noon into three equal parts, and place the rule <note>The pivoting pointer or "label" on the front of the astrolabe</note> on the end of the first part, and you will have in the Zodiac the commencement of the twelfth house; and the <term>nadir</term> <note>The point on the zodiac exactly opposite (180 degrees) from a given degree</note> or opposite part of this degree will show you the sixth house. # ANOTHER METHOD TO
### find and erect the twelve artificial houses of the heavens.

The ancient astrologers divided the sky into twelve parts following the twelve signs, which are called <term>houses</term> <note>Divisions of the celestial sphere that represent different aspects of life in an astrological chart.</note>, of which there are perpetually six above the horizon and another six below. The properties of these shall be declared in the twenty-eighth and final chapter. These houses can be made in various ways, but we shall follow that of the learned <term>Johannes Regiomontanus</term> <note>original: "Ioannes de monte regio"; a 15th-century German mathematician and astronomer whose system of house division became the European standard.</note>, as it is the most common. If you wish, then, to know how to <term>domify</term> <note>The technical act of calculating and placing the twelve houses in an astrological chart.</note> by your astrolabe at any hour—which is to find in which of these twelve parts the twelve celestial signs are located—first know the <term>equal hour</term> <note>Standard 60-minute hours, as used by clocks, rather than seasonal hours.</note> and minute, for both day and night. Set the straight line of the <term>rule</term> <note>The rotating bar or pointer on the back or front of the astrolabe.</note> or small rule of your astrolabe to that same hour and minute; then, without moving it, [turn] the <term>rete</term> <note>original: "araigne"; the pierced, rotating plate on the front of the astrolabe that maps the stars and the zodiac.</note> until you have placed the degree where the Sun is on that day under the straight line of your rule. Once this is done, look at which signs are within the twelve houses, and especially the sign and degree that will be on the <term>meridian line</term> <note>The vertical line on the astrolabe plate representing the Midheaven or noon position.</note>, for by this you can easily domify. When houses are not marked on a particular astrolabe, you shall observe, at the hour you wish to domify, the sign and degree that will be on the meridian line, having positioned your <term>Rete</term> <note>original: "Aranea ou Reth"</note>,
